subject: geography
title: Feedback Loops & Anthropogenic Disruption
welcome_lead: Trace positive and negative feedbacks driving cycle change.
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on feedback mechanisms and human impacts on water and carbon cycles.
final_note: Feedbacks amplify or dampen cycle responses to disturbance.

concepts.def: Initial change is amplified, e.g. ice-albedo loop accelerating melt.
Initial change is dampened, e.g. increased CO2 boosting plant growth that absorbs CO2.
Melting ice exposes darker surface, absorbs more heat, drives further melt.
Releases stored methane and CO2, amplifying warming.
Reduces evapotranspiration and carbon sequestration; Amazon losing ~10000 km^2/yr.
Rising CO2 lowers ocean pH (from 8.2 pre-industrial to ~8.1 today).

walkthroughs.body_html: Arctic sea-ice loss reduces albedo from about 0.8 to 0.06 for open water, absorbing more solar energy and amplifying warming. Permafrost holds around 1500 Gt of carbon; thawing releases methane (~25x CO2 warming potential over 100 years).
CO2 fertilisation can increase plant productivity, sequestering extra carbon. Increased evaporation forms more clouds which can raise albedo. These dampening effects are limited and may saturate.

Fossil fuel burning adds ~10 Gt C/yr; land-use change adds ~1.5 Gt C/yr. Urbanisation reduces infiltration, increases surface runoff and flood risk. Atmospheric CO2 has risen from 280 ppm (1750) to over 420 ppm (2024).
